pairs.why: B's diagonal stripes get a soft lighter glow behind the maps, like the real card's lit-center stripe field; A's stripes are flatter.
B keeps the scenery to a few large quiet shapes (hills, a plain track), while A adds more shrubs, rocks, a mesa and grass tufts around the train.
Both have the same moon-surface ledge with scattered rocks and craters and the same ray backdrop, so staging gives no reason to choose.
A's diamonds are larger and fewer, like the real card's quiet tone-on-tone pattern; B's are smaller and busier, though both use a similar plain ledge.
Both float the umbrella on the same concentric-ring field, with no props and no difference in staging.
A's pi pattern is slightly sparser and larger like the real one, while B's is a bit denser and more crowded around the hero.
B has less clutter: thin railing, no big yellow support and no rivets, and a quieter pool edge. A's busier structure and splash add detail the real card does not have.
B keeps the clock hanging on a plain striped wall with a soft drop shadow, as the real card does; A invents a floor ledge with a cast shadow under it.
